_comment: GOLDEN-REGENERATION INTEGRITY GATE — provenance allowlist (issue #122).
Goldens/vectors are self-produced by the implementation-under-test. This file
is how a PR carries an INDEPENDENT justification for changing one. Every entry
pins a specific golden file to the exact NEW content it is authorizing, via a
sha256 of that file's bytes. Because the pin is content-addressed, an entry can
only ever justify the ONE value it was reviewed for — a later, different
regeneration of the same file fails the gate again and forces a fresh entry.
See conformance/README.md -> 'Golden-regeneration integrity gate' for the full
design and the two ways to satisfy the gate.
Schema of each entry in `entries`:
path             (string, required)  repo-root-relative path of the golden file
sha256           (string, required)  hex sha256 of the file's NEW (post-change) bytes
verified-against (enum,   required)  one of: official-KAT | second-implementation |
differential-oracle | intentional-spec-change
reason           (string, required)  human explanation of WHY the new bytes are correct
and against WHICH independent oracle they were checked
reviewer         (string, required)  sign-off marker, e.g. a GitHub handle 'gh:alice'
date             (string, optional)  ISO date the entry was added
To compute the sha256 of a golden after you have regenerated it:
shasum -a 256 conformance/tests/<fixture>/expected-script.hex
or run the checker with --print-hashes to get them for the whole changed set.

Regenerated for deep-review finding C27 (else-present N-field stack reconcile). spend()'s len(scratch)-driven if/else writes BOTH state fields (count:bigint + tag:ByteString) on each arm; the pre-fix 05-stack-lower N-result reconcile was gated on empty-else, so this else-present multi-field write fell through to a single stackMap name for N results and emitted an unspendable OP_NUM2BIN continuation (silently uniform across all 7 tiers — parity-green-but-wrong). The fix broadens the reconcile to the else-present path, growing the script +5 bytes (1081->1086). Verified against the differential-execution oracle: conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/branched-readonly-len.json drives deploy->call->@bsv/sdk Spend for BOTH branches (count 5->6/tag->4142 and count 5->4/tag->3030) plus a tampered-output reject — all validate. Also corroborated by 7-tier cross-compiler byte-identical parity (fold-off and fold-on).

These bytes are the regenerated output of that fix. INDEPENDENT ORACLE: the emitted script is executed against the real @bsv/sdk interpreter in packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/ec-add-doubling.test.ts and checked against the known secp256k1 group elements — ecAdd(G,2G)==3G (chord path unchanged), ecAdd(G,G)==2G and ecAdd(2G,2G)==4G (doubling fixed), with ecMulGen(3)==3G as a control. The original defect was first observed as a real regtest-node rejection of the ec-unit fixture. Cross-tier: conformance 65/65 with no tier-vs-tier divergence; Zig and Go verified byte-identical on the same ecAdd ANF.

Re-stamped after the ecAdd doubling fix. Only the five EC fixtures moved, by +0.05%..+0.09% (convergence-proof, ec-demo, ec-primitives, ec-unit, schnorr-zkp) — the tangent-slope selection adds 124 ops and reuses the single existing fieldInv. All 60 other fixtures are byte-unchanged.

ecMul / ecMulGen returned the ALL-ZERO point for the scalar k = 2 exactly. The Jacobian ladder adds the affine P to the accumulator; at the last step the accumulator is (k'-1)*P with k' = k + 3n, which for k = 2 IS P, and the mixed-add cannot double: H = U2 - X1 = 0 makes Z3 = Z1*H = 0 and fieldInv is Fermat, so fieldInv(0) = 0 and the Jacobian->affine conversion yields 64 zero bytes instead of 2P. Any contract multiplying by 2 deployed an UNSPENDABLE script, byte-identically across all seven tiers. The last step now computes both the mixed-add and the doubling of the saved accumulator and branchlessly selects on (H == 0 AND R == 0). Only the last step needs it: c_i = k' >> i ranges over a contiguous interval fixed by i, so exhaustive interval arithmetic over the whole domain k in [0, n-1] shows the only reachable exceptional steps are i = 0 for k = 2 (accumulator == P, the bug) and i = 0 for k = 0 (accumulator == -P, result infinity, unchanged). These bytes are the regenerated output of that fix. Two defects in the NIST P-256 / P-384 codegen, both fund-safety. (1) cAffineAdd implemented only the chord slope (qy-py)/(qx-px), which is 0/0 when P == Q, so p256Add(P,P) and p384Add(P,P) produced a WRONG point — the tangent-select that 8a6494b4 applied to secp256k1 was never ported to the a = -3 curves, where the tangent numerator is 3px^2 - 3. (2) The scalar ladder's Jacobian mixed-add cannot double, so p256Mul(P,2n) / p384Mul(P,2n) returned 64 / 96 ZERO bytes (H = 0 -> Z3 = 0 -> Fermat inv(0) = 0). Both now fixed: the affine add selects tangent numerator/denominator before the single cFieldInv, and the ladder's last step selects between the mixed-add and a doubling on (H == 0 AND R == 0). Exhaustive interval arithmetic over k in [0, n-1] shows i = 0 is the only reachable exceptional step on either curve (cofactor 1, so every on-curve P has order n and the caller cannot move the exception). These bytes are the regenerated output of both fixes. INDEPENDENT ORACLE: packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/p256-p384-point-ops.test.ts executes the emitted script through the real @bsv/sdk Spend interpreter and compares every result against OPENSSL — Node's crypto.createECDH('prime256v1' / 'secp384r1') with the scalar set as the private key, whose derived public key is k*G — for k = 1,2,3,4,7, n-1 and a pseudorandom scalar, plus pNNNAdd(G,G)==2G, pNNNAdd(3G,3G)==6G, and the chord controls pNNNAdd(G,2G)==3G / pNNNAdd(2G,5G)==7G. A from-scratch double-and-add written from the curve parameters alone is cross-checked against OpenSSL first. The interpreter's p256*/p384* MOCKS (constant zero point, unconditional true on-curve) were replaced with real arithmetic in the same change, so the differential oracle is no longer vacuous for these fixtures. Cross-tier: all 7 tiers produce byte-identical hex in BOTH fold modes; sha256 of every tier's output equals the sha256 pinned here.

Re-stamped after the ecMul/ecMulGen k=2 fix (secp256k1) and the p256Add/p384Add doubling + p256Mul/p384Mul k=2 fixes (NIST). Only the nine EC fixtures moved, all by +0.21%..+0.33%: convergence-proof +1151 B (+0.255%), ec-demo +3453 B (+0.260%), ec-primitives +3453 B (+0.260%), ec-unit +1151 B (+0.254%), p256-primitives +3025 B (+0.327%), p256-wallet +3025 B (+0.317%), p384-primitives +4049 B (+0.216%), p384-wallet +4049 B (+0.207%), schnorr-zkp +2302 B (+0.264%). All 57 other fixtures are byte-unchanged. The growth is bounded because the exceptional case is handled at the ladder's LAST step only, which is provably the only reachable one; handling it at every step was measured at +70%..+73% (ecMul 427,536 -> 726,618 B; p256Mul 458,464 -> 794,040 B; p384Mul 925,653 -> 1,594,684 B) and was rejected on that basis.
